title: Numerical analysis
audience: a college student in a mathematics degree program (or a related major such as physics, computer science or economics), or an adult studying the same material on their own
purpose: Learn how computers solve mathematical problems and how to trust the answers: floating-point arithmetic and error, conditioning and stability, root finding, interpolation and polynomial approximation, numerical differentiation and integration, direct methods for linear systems, least squares, iterative and eigenvalue methods, and numerical methods for ordinary differential equations, with convergence proofs and Python throughout.
primary_reading: Fundamentals of Numerical Computation by Tobin A. Driscoll and Richard J. Braun, Python edition (free online)

weeks.3: Root finding: bisection, fixed-point iteration and Newton's method
weeks.5: Polynomial interpolation and the Runge phenomenon
weeks.8: Numerical integration: trapezoid, Simpson and Gaussian quadrature
weeks.9: Gaussian elimination, LU factorization and pivoting
weeks.10: Condition numbers, least squares and QR factorization
weeks.11: Iterative methods and the power method
weeks.12: Euler and Runge–Kutta methods for differential equations

blocks.deliverable: Measure the cancellation error in a supplied formula and rewrite the formula stably.
Implement Newton's method and measure its order of convergence.
Compare equispaced and Chebyshev interpolation of a supplied function.
Week 7 midterm; verify the orders of the trapezoid and Simpson rules.
Solve a supplied system and bound its error with the condition number.
Implement a Runge–Kutta method and verify its order.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Numerical methods library: write a tested plain-Python library with Newton's method, Chebyshev interpolation, adaptive Simpson integration, LU factorization with partial pivoting and the classical fourth-order Runge–Kutta method, verify each method's order of convergence numerically in tables, and write a report that proves two of the error bounds and explains one case where a method fails.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
